title: Tidy-Up Games
strapline: The same song every time, a basket to fill, everything home to its picture-labelled shelf — tidy-up as the last, best game.
intent: Make tidying-up a genuine part of the play — a shared, satisfying game rather than a chore imposed at the end.
Grow the sorting, matching and classifying that live inside putting-away — all the cars here, every block home to its shelf.
Build belonging and responsibility as toddlers care for their room and see that their help really matters.
Feed the transporting and posting schemas that make tidy-up genuinely appealing to this age.
Support the language of routine and category — 'home time for the blocks', 'where does this one belong?'.
implementation: Use a consistent tidy-up cue every time — the same song, bell or countdown — so children learn the rhythm and join in.
Label shelves and baskets with photos and outlines so every toy has a visible home a toddler can match it to.
Turn it into a game — 'can you find everything red?', 'race the basket to the shelf', 'post all the animals home'.
Give real, doable jobs and thank the effort specifically ('you put every single car away — the shelf looks brilliant').
Allow enough time and keep it warm, never a punishment; tidy alongside the children rather than commanding from the side.
key_questions: Where does this one belong — can you find its home?
Can you find everything that's round to put away?
Shall we fill the basket right up before we carry it?
Which shelf does the picture match?
How quickly can we make the room lovely again?

impact.text: Toddlers sort and group as they tidy — all the cars together, every block matched home to its labelled shelf.
Children follow the tidy-up cue and simple instructions — 'put the animals in the basket' — joining the routine.
Tidying becomes shared work, toddlers filling baskets and carrying alongside their friends.
The transporting urge is happily fed — bags filled, baskets hauled, toys posted home to their shelves.

enhancements: A signature tidy-up song or bell used the same way every single time.
Photo-and-outline labels on every shelf and basket so toys have a visible home.
Baskets and trolleys to fill and transport the toys away.
A sorting challenge — colour, shape or type — built into the putting-away.
A 'sparkle checker' round at the end so children spot and fix the last few strays.

playing_exploring: Children treat tidy-up as a game, exploring sorting, matching and carrying with real enthusiasm.
Filling, transporting and posting toys home engage the whole body.
active_learning: Toddlers stick with the job to the end, proud of a room they helped make lovely again.
creating_thinking: Children decide where each thing belongs and work out how to match it to its labelled home.
